newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says Japan okays transgenic canola imports.
newsitem.headline: Canada says Japan okays transgenic canola imports.

text.p: Canada on Wednesday said Japan approved the environmental, food and feed safety of three Canadian lines of transgenic canola, opening the door to Canadian commercial exports.

"I am extremely pleased with the timely assessment and approval this issue has received from the government of Japan," Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said in a news release. "The decision is good news for Canadian seed producers and exporters, for Japanese importers and for the economies of both countries."
Tokyo's decision came after a Canadian trade mission to Japan in April in which Goodale discussed future Japanese imports of Canadian transgenic canola.

Transgenic canola is a type of seed that has been altered through the insertion of a gene from another species into the canola plant, Agriculture Canada said. The three types of transgenic canola approved by Japan have a trait that provides them with tolerance to specific herbicides.

Canada approved the marketing of these types of transgenic canola in early 1995 after environmental, food and safety reviews. About 200,000 acres, or 2.0 percent of Canada's total Canola crop was sown with transgenic canola in 1996.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
